content_type.description: The mime type of the file.
content_type.title: Content Type

file_name.description: The name of the file. It will be auto-generated if not provided.
file_name.title: File Name

file_size.description: The size of the file in bytes.
file_size.title: File Size

url.description: The URL where the file can be downloaded from.
url.title: Url

PresetCustomization.description:
Runtime customization of a preset. Fields are Optional all the way down
so this block can sit under the playground's 'Additional Settings' section
without flagging required-field asterisks the user didn't ask for.

position.description: Vertical placement of static subtitles on screen.
position.title: Position

shadow.description: Improves readability over bright or busy backgrounds.
shadow.title: Shadow

text_customizations.description: Per-tier text styling for baseline and highlighted words.
text_customizations.title: Text customizations

PresetCustomization.title: PresetCustomization

customization.description: Optional preset overrides: vertical position, shadow intensity, and per-tier text styling (font, weight, hex colour) for each word-importance tier. Any omitted field keeps the preset's default.

language.description: Improves transcription accuracy, and should match the source audio (not output subtitles).
language.title: Language

preset.description:
Each style defines fonts, colors, layout, and animation. Two tiers with different pricing:

- Dynamic presets (2x multiplier): glass, whisper, glide2, fusion, glide, terminal, handwritten, backdrop, backdrop2. Richer, context-aware rendering that adapts to the input.
- Basic presets (1x multiplier): simple, plain, beans, corpo, boo, shadeplay, casper, capri, lowkey, vinta, diego, ali, slay, kitty, hustle, karl, sprout, flex, mint, rizz, vegas. Fixed, lightweight styling with predictable output.
preset.title: Preset

srt_content.description: Paste raw SRT subtitle text. Alternative to srt_file_url. When provided, transcription is skipped.
srt_content.title: SRT Content

srt_file_url.description: Upload or paste a URL to your .srt subtitles file. When provided, transcription is skipped.
srt_file_url.title: SRT File Url

translation_language.description: Translate the subtitles into this language. Omit to keep the original spoken language. If you also pass srt_content or srt_file_url, set `language` to its source language for the most reliable translation.
translation_language.title: Translation Language

video_url.description: Upload or paste a URL to the video you want to subtitle.
video_url.title: Video Url

vocabulary.description: Optional list of terms to help auto-transcription correctly recognise brand names and domain jargon that providers commonly mis-spell (e.g. "VEED" → "vid"). Ignored when srt_content / srt_file_url is set.
vocabulary.title: Vocabulary

TextCustomization.description: Per-tier text overrides. No italic field (preset-dictated, see ENR-2516).

color.description: Override the text color for this tier.
color.title: Color

font.description: Override the font used for this text tier. Must be a supported Google Font — see https://www.veed.io/api/v1/subtitle-renders/fonts for the canonical list. Unrecognized fonts are rejected with a 400.
font.title: Font

weight.description: Font weight 100-900. Values >= 700 render as bold
weight.title: Weight

TextCustomization.title: TextCustomization

TextCustomizations.description: Text customization keyed by word-importance tier.

baseline.description: Baseline styling applied to every word in the transcript. This is what a reader sees by default, before any per-word emphasis is applied.
baseline.title: Baseline (all words)

highlighted.description: Mid-rank words (automatically marked as noteworthy: key nouns, action verbs, salient adjectives). Presets typically bump size or weight on these.
highlighted.title: Highlighted (mid-rank)

TextCustomizations.title: TextCustomizations

VocabularyEntry.description: A term auto-transcription should recognise correctly, plus its common misspellings.

replaces.description: Misspellings that should be replaced with `word`. Matched whole-word and case-insensitively — list each misspelling once; you don't need to enumerate casings (e.g. `['vid']` already covers `Vid`, `VID`).
replaces.title: Replaces

word.description: The correctly-spelled term. Brand names, product names, and domain jargon work best.
word.title: Word

VocabularyEntry.title: VocabularyEntry
